(Reuters) -- Federal Reserve chief nominee Kevin Warsh said on Tuesday he had made no promises to President Donald Trump about cutting interest rates, as he tried to assure U.S.', 'Coupled with the implications of artificial intelligence for jobs and prices, he said he would move quickly to see if new data tools could provide better insight on inflation, and also to discourage policymakers from saying too much about where interest rates might be heading.', 'In a hearing that ranged from Warsh\'s calls for "regime change" at the Fed to contentious exchanges over his personal finances, the 56-year-old lawyer and financier said that in his conversations with Trump about the job, "the president never asked me to commit to interest rate cuts ...', '"Too many Fed officials opine about where interest rates should be.', "Tillis' hold on the nomination could leave Warsh unconfirmed and Powell remaining as Fed chief even after his tenure in the top job ends on May 15.", 'The Fed has missed its 2% inflation goal for more than five years, first due to the shock of the pandemic and the combination of supply chain disruptions and fiscal spending triggered by it, but more recently due to the influence of Trump administration tariffs and the high oil prices linked to the war in the Middle East.', "Thom Tillis, in an unusual turn, used his time during the hearing not to ask questions of Warsh but to detail why he would delay the confirmation until the Trump administration drops an ongoing criminal probe of current Fed Chair Jerome Powell over a renovation of the central bank's It could come back to bite him', 'url': 'https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/22/kevin-warsh-inflation-trend-pce-trump.html', 'source': 'CNBC', 'publishedAt': '2026-04-22T18:00:46Z', 'key_sentences': ["Kevin Warsh, President Donald Trump's nominee for Federal Reserve chair, told lawmakers that he would like the central bank to change its strategy for measuring inflation.", '"This is ironic because Warsh also argued yesterday for looking through one-off, supply-driven price increases."
In other words, by trimming only the most extreme readings, some more minor spikes in inflation — perhaps caused by food and energy prices jumping — could creep into the inflation reading under Warsh's method and cause it to be higher than the Fed's current preferred view.', '"We take out all of the tail-risks, all of the one-off items, and we ask ourselves whether the generalized change in prices is having second-order effects on the economy."
Under Warsh's system, Bank of America's Bhave said, inflation today does look softer.', "During Tuesday's hearing, Warsh pushed back on the idea that he would lower interest rates solely at the request of Trump.", 'But Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave warned Wednesday that such a reconfiguration — part of a broader "regime change" that Warsh has promised for the central bank — might not pan out as he hopes.', 'The Fed has long favored the core price index for personal consumption expenditures, known in short as the core PCE, because it excludes volatile food and energy prices.', 'If trimmed inflation outpaced the core PCE in the future, Bhave said, Warsh would likely have to stand by his view, tying his hands.'], 'sentiment_score': np.float64(-0.5303450626102824), 'article_weight': np.float64(0.4440509155874041)}, {'title': "Where to Invest With the US Economy at Risk of 'Overheating': Citi", 'url': 'https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/where-to-invest-us-economy-inflation-overheating-growth-stocks-citi-2026-4', 'source': 'Markets Insider', 'publishedAt': '2026-04-22T17:26:30Z', 'key_sentences': ['Cyclical stocks
Cyclical stocks, which tend to do well when the economy is growing, are expected to hold up across most "overheating" scenarios, barring a scenario in which economic growth is strong but "not exceptional," Citi said.', '"Our findings suggest that Value isn't always a universe inflation hedge but works when growth expectations exist (Overheating)," analysts wrote.', '- Citi shared its best investment ideas as it sees the US economy at risk of overheating.', 'Concerns over inflation have swelled since the start of the Iran war, which has caused the price of oil, a major economic input that could influence inflation in other areas, to soar.', '- The bank sees signs that markets are shifting from an ideal state to one where growth & inflation are hot.', '"With inflation risk elevated and the economic transmission of the energy shock still playing out, we examine what these binding constraints mean for factor performance," analysts said.', 'The US economy could be in tricky territory, Citi analysts are warning.'], 'sentiment_score': np.float64(0.7520763205556774), 'article_weight': np.float64(1.4294941257905125)}, {'title': 'Why Elon Musk Is Right and Wrong About Inflation Risk From AI Checks', 'url': 'https://www.businessinsider.com/elon-musk-steve-hanke-universal-high-income-inflation-ai-unemployment-2026-4', 'source': 'Business Insider', 'publishedAt': '2026-04-22T10:51:00Z', 'key_sentences': ['- Elon Musk said government checks for all could address job losses from AI without causing inflation.', 'The index measures "misery" by factoring in a country's unemployment, inflation, interest rates, and real GDP per capita.', 'The Tesla and SpaceX CEO headed off concerns that doling out big checks would drive up prices: "AI/robotics will produce goods & services far in excess of the increase in the money supply, so there will not be inflation."
In other words, Musk believes that AI and robotics will supercharge production and push down prices, offsetting the inflationary impact of the government boosting the money supply when it pays large [{'title': "Stock Investors in Their 'Own Universe' Where AI Trumps All: Gordon", 'url': 'https://www.businessinsider.com/stock-market-outlook-ai-bubble-iran-war-unemployment-allbirds-gordon-2026-4', 'source': 'Business Insider', 'publishedAt': '2026-04-23T10:30:06Z', 'key_sentences': ['"The market shrugs off war in the Middle East, inflation, wild oil prices, and tens of thousands of job cuts," the entrepreneurship professor told Business Insider.', 'The S&P 500 has surged more than 10% to all-time highs this month, despite the US-Iran war disrupting international trade and energy flows, catapulting oil prices to four-year highs, and threatening to choke global economic growth and reignite inflation.', 'Stock investors are living in a parallel reality where AI trumps everything, and threats can be safely ignored, Erik Gordon says.', "- Investors are so detached from reality that they're living in their own universe, Erik Gordon says.", '"It fabricated its own universe where the only things that are real are companies with 'AI' in their name," he added.', 'Whether Gordon is right that the stock market is disconnected from reality, or investors are looking past the current chaos and correctly pricing in vast future returns from AI, will only become clear over time.', '- The stock market "shrugs off" war, oil shocks, and job losses, the entrepreneurship professor said.'], 'sentiment_score': np.float64(0.15725744168001093), 'article_weight': np.float64(1.3068494999410245)}, {'title': 'Inflation First, Reforms Ahead: Breaking Down Kevin Warsh’s Fed Chair Hearing', 'url': 'https://www.investing.com/analysis/inflation-first-reforms-ahead-breaking-down-kevin-warshs-fed-chair-hearing-200679023', 'source': 'Investing.com', 'publishedAt': '2026-04-23T09:39:59Z', 'key_sentences': ['He wants a broad overhaul:
- New inflation framework/measurement approach
- Overhauled Communications—less forward guidance (he called it "unhelpful"), more open debate, "messier" FOMC meetings with real dissent instead of scripted consensus
- Narrower Remit: Fed should "stay in its lane" on monetary policy and avoid fiscal/social policy overreach
- Smaller balance sheet over time, a long-held Warsh view
- Less reliance on academic models/groupthink.', 'Assuming he finally gets through, Warsh would likely steer the Fed in a meaningfully different direction than the Powell era, but not a wild lurch:
Overall stance: data-dependent but with a reformed "reaction function." Historically Warsh has leaned hawkish, but his growth optimism gives him a dovish channel on rates if productivity data cooperates.', 'Bullish On Growth/Productivity
He highlighted the AI and tech boom as potentially raising the economy’s potential growth rate and neutral interest rate, similar to the 1990s productivity surge, which could create room for lower rates without reigniting inflation.', 'military seizes another vessel linked to Iran amid ongoing Mideast tensions
Kevin Warsh’s Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing yesterday (21 April 2026) was the big event—he’s President Trump’s nominee to replace Jerome Powell as Fed Chair.', 'It was a fiery, high-stakes session focused on independence, inflation, his personal finances, and his vision for overhauling how the Fed operates.', 'He criticised past Fed errors, especially 2020-era policy that let inflation "take hold".', '- More hawkish tilt on inflation control initially, with a stronger "no excuses" accountability culture.'], 'sentiment_score': np.float64(0.5541542346633257), 'article_weight': np.float64(0.9942274651013706)}]
